lectures.label: A
lectures.title: Dental Endocrinology Clinical Application
lectures.note: Taught November 6 and moved here from Exam 2 (Dr. Herr left it off Exam 2), with everything the Exam 2 hub had for it.

likelyTopics.t: Hypoglycemia in the chair: the signs, a finger-stick (some CGMs stop reading at a floor), straight glucose rather than table sugar, a slow response on a GLP-1 drug, glucagon IM or subcutaneously if oral glucose fails

Before treating a diabetic: HbA1c above 7 is poorly controlled (implant failure, periodontal disease), confirm the meal and medication, morning appointments; Dr. Taylor's metformin with a skipped breakfast; pack-years
Hyperthyroidism and Graves disease (his first case): epinephrine caution, and thyroid storm (fever, pulse 140 or more; call 911)
Addison disease (his third case): oral pigment from high ACTH, adrenal crisis triggers and signs, extra corticosteroid after a big procedure; Cushing syndrome and long-term steroids
Hyperparathyroidism on the radiograph (lost lamina dura, radiolucent brown tumors, mobility) and the calcium regulators (PTH, vitamin D, calcitonin)
Acromegaly's growing jaw (Class I to Class III, diastemas, macroglossia); growth plates fused by the sex hormones, and implant timing
The three hormone classes with examples, receptors, and endocrine versus nervous signaling
Diabetes: type 1 versus type 2 (insulin ineffective, not deficient), oral manifestations and the sugar in saliva, the two-way periodontal link, SGLT2 drugs and UTIs
Hyperthyroid versus hypothyroid dental considerations (hypothyroidism far more common), and the recurrent laryngeal nerve in thyroid surgery
Sex hormones and the mouth: puberty, pregnancy gingivitis and the interproximal pyogenic granuloma, menopause
Pituitary hormones (ADH and diabetes insipidus), alpha and beta cells, and the adrenal medulla

hCG rescues the corpus luteum: made by the trophoblasts, it keeps the corpus luteum making progesterone and estrogen through the first trimester, LH and FSH stay suppressed, and it is what a pregnancy test measures
Prolactin makes the milk and oxytocin lets it down through the myoepithelial cells; during pregnancy progesterone antagonizes prolactin, so full milk production waits for delivery
Dopamine tonically inhibits prolactin; suckling lowers dopamine and raises oxytocin from the posterior pituitary; prolactin inhibits GnRH, so periods stop
Fertilization: ZP3 sets off the acrosomal reaction, the sperm then binds ZP2, the oocyte finishes its second meiotic division, and the cortical reaction blocks polyspermy

The pregnancy steroids: estriol is the estrogen of pregnancy; the placenta makes progesterone on its own but needs the fetal adrenal's 17,20 desmolase and the fetal liver before its aromatase makes estriol

Labor: the estrogen-to-progesterone ratio rises; uterine distention, prostaglandins (PGF2 alpha for contraction, PGE2 for the cervix) and oxytocin from the posterior pituitary; oxytocin limits bleeding after delivery
The placenta's other hormones: human placental lactogen opposes insulin (an insulin-resistant, hyperinsulinemic pregnancy and gestational diabetes); relaxin keeps the uterus quiet
Implantation at the blastocyst stage: trophoblasts, cytotrophoblasts (nurse cells) versus syncytiotrophoblasts (invasion), and decidualization
Capacitation: why ejaculated sperm can't fertilize yet, and the membrane changes that make the acrosomal reaction possible
Maternal hormones that promote fertilization: estrogen at ovulation helps the sperm, then holds the embryo back until progesterone relaxes the myometrium
The endocrine basis of contraception: the pill blunts the LH surge, progestin thickens the cervical mucus, high-dose estrogen prevents implantation
